# Independent audit: unequal sampling, canonical lattice lifts, and parity-budget attainment

Auditor: research-agent. Date: 2026-09-19.



Sources audited directly:

* `candidate 640d07cd1de2a423`;
* `candidate b11292bf5c80c58d`;
* `candidate 2086e4eaa4bce465`.

The compactness dependencies were checked in `candidate c280bb0dcfd30f3d`, `candidate dbf3b23d25004153`, and the two elementary normalization lemmas in `candidate 2a5bf571e6159901`. The current scope was checked against `historical context (not an accepted premise)`.

## 1. Rectangle--simplex counterexample

Here (t=1/100), (A=[1/100,27/100]\times[1/100,26/100]), (B=\Delta_2), and (D=(21/20)\Delta_2). Their areas are

\[
(a,b,c)=(13/200,1/2,441/800),\qquad M=893/800.
\]

The endpoint sections of their three-fiber convex hull are exactly the supplied endpoint bodies because the base endpoints are exposed. At the middle base, an arbitrary convex combination with middle coefficient \(\eta\) has endpoint coefficients \((1-t)(1-\eta)\) and \(t(1-\eta)\). Its continuous section is therefore contained in the convex hull of (B) and ((1-t)A+tD). The latter lies strictly inside (B): both coordinates are positive and the maximum coordinate sum is

\[
(99/100)(53/100)+(1/100)(21/20)=669/1250<1.
\]

Thus all three supplied bodies are actual positive sections. Their hull has ambient interior, since it joins full-dimensional continuous fibers over a nondegenerate base interval.

For the middle caps in source equation (3), the margins sum identically to zero on (z=t), so their union covers the entire candidate plane, including all equality cases. Their masses are respectively

\[
13/200+9/50=49/200,\quad49/200,\quad49/200.
\]

At (z=0), the first cap contains (A), while the other thresholds are (7/25>27/100,26/100). At (z=1), all three restrictions miss (D) strictly. Hence no omitted side-fiber mass enters these computations.

The two first-plane caps in source equation (5) have opposite margins on that plane and cut (A) at (x=7/50), its exact horizontal midpoint. They exclude the other fibers and each have mass (13/400). The three last-plane caps in source equation (6) again have margin sum zero, exclude the other fibers, and each have area (49/200). All normal coefficients are nonzero ambient normals; the displayed integer/continuous couplings are retained.

Consequently every candidate belongs to an explicit closed cap of mass at most (Q=49/200). Conversely the actual last-fiber centroid ((1,7/20,7/20)) has raw depth at least ((4/9)c=Q) from that fiber alone, by ordinary Grünbaum. If an ambient halfspace has zero continuous normal, its restriction to a fiber containing its centroid is the entire fiber, so this lower bound includes that case. Nonzero continuous restrictions are closed planar halfspaces and are covered by the same ordinary theorem. Therefore

\[
D=Q/M=196/893,\qquad 2/9-D=22/8037>0.
\]

The finite base has Helly number two: every nonempty convex trace on three ordered collinear sites is an interval trace; the trace with the greatest first site and the trace with the smallest last site already determine emptiness. Disjoint singleton traces give the converse inequality. Thus this is an exact counterexample to the *arbitrary sampled-base* (gamma_2/h(P)) claim.

## 2. OC-safe projective preimage

At consecutive integer bases (0,1,2), use (198A,100B,2D). The only nontrivial middle inclusion is

\[
\tfrac12(198A)+\tfrac12(2D)=99A+D\subset100B,
\]

which is precisely the preceding inclusion multiplied by 100. Thus these are actual sections; the projection is ([0,2]), with no other integer bases. Their total mass is

\[
198^2(13/200)+100^2/2+2^2(441/800)
=1510093/200<10000.
\]

The middle fiber has mass 5000, greater than half the total. Its own centroid therefore proves the (n=1,d=2) OC bound for this entire source, for every ambient halfspace.

The projective denominator (L(z)=198-98z) is positive on the whole projection, with values (198,100,2). The map

\[
F(z,x,y)=(z,x,y)/L(z)
\]

has a nonsingular homogeneous matrix. More explicitly its inverse on the image chart is ((z',x',y')\mapsto198(z',x',y')/(1+98z')). For positive denominators,

\[
F\Big(\sum_i\lambda_iw_i\Big)
=\sum_i\frac{\lambda_iL(w_i)}{\sum_j\lambda_jL(w_j)}F(w_i).
\]

Thus it maps the entire source hull to the hull of its three fiber images, not merely the listed sites. Those images have bases (0,1/100,1) and bodies exactly (A,B,D). Within a fixed fiber its area factor is (L(z)^{-2}), which differs at the three sites. Hence unweighted depth need not be preserved.

No affine-lattice completeness is hidden here. A rank-one affine lattice meets any interval in consecutive equally spaced points. Three such points cannot have adjacent spacing ratio (1:99). Scaling the displayed sites to (0,1,100) introduces all intermediate positive actual integer fibers. The example is therefore not an OC counterexample.

## 3. Homothetic-simplex counterexample

For radii (5/19,1,39/38) at (0,t,1), the two interpolating slopes are exactly (1400/19) and (50/1881), positive and decreasing. The section radius of the convex hull is therefore their piecewise affine interpolation. Equivalently the sole nontrivial anchored average has radius (1029/3800<1). All sections stated in the source are actual, positive, homothetic simplices with one common vertex.

The three areas and their total are

\[
(25/722,1/2,1521/2888),\qquad M=3065/2888.
\]

The three middle-plane margins sum to zero. Their own-fiber areas are (144/722,169/722,169/722); only the first receives the first-fiber mass (25/722), and none receives last-fiber mass. Thus each mixed cap has (Q=169/722). The first-plane isolating triple has mass (50/3249<Q) in each cap, and the last-plane triple has mass (Q) in each cap. Both triples cover their whole candidate planes by exact zero margin sums. All side-fiber exclusions in the source are strict.

The actual last-fiber centroid is ((1,13/38,13/38)). Ordinary Grünbaum gives raw depth at least ((4/9)(1521/2888)=Q), including all oblique and pure-base ambient halfspaces as above. The nine-cap upper cover gives equality:

\[
D=676/3065,\qquad2/9-D=46/27585>0.
\]

Thus concave positive radius, common shape, and common vertex do not repair arbitrary sampling. The failure remains outside lattice-complete sampling.

## 4. Integer canonical graph and saturated lattice

For finite lattice-complete (U\subset\mathbb Z^n), every anchored representation polytope is a rational bounded polytope. Its finite rational vertices suffice to impose all Jensen equalities on (f:U\to\mathbb R). Hence (L(U)) is a rational kernel and has a rational basis. Scaling added basis functions to integer values gives an injective integer graph

\[
\Psi(u)=(u,f_1(u),\ldots,f_k(u)).
\]

The constant and graph coordinate functions span (L(U)), so this graph and the canonical lift are affinely equivalent on their affine hulls. This does not assert that the graph projection is invertible on the original ambient space; the needed inverse only relates the two canonical realizations.

If an integer (w\in\operatorname{conv}\Psi(U)) projects to (u), lattice completeness gives (u\in U). The convex combination producing (w) is now an anchored representation at (u), so all added coordinates equal (f_j(u)). Thus

\[
\operatorname{conv}\Psi(U)\cap\mathbb Z^{n+k}=\Psi(U).
\]

The direction space (E_0) of its affine hull is spanned by integer differences. The subgroup (Lambda_0=E_0\cap\mathbb Z^{n+k}) is discrete, has the full rank (dim E_0), and is saturated. The source's primitive-vector induction is valid: an ambient unimodular change sends a primitive member to (e_1); subtracting its first coordinate splits off (mathbb Ze_1), leaving a saturated subgroup in the remaining coordinates. Induction gives a lattice basis of (Lambda_0). Translation by one graph point gives a full-rank affine lattice in the graph's affine hull. The rank-zero case is a singleton.

Closed minors are lattice-complete: an integer point of their hull first belongs to the larger complete set, and closedness then puts it in the minor. The same remains true successively. For an original convex mixed source, its positive-(d)-volume bases are lattice-complete: any integer convex combination of such bases contains a translate of a positive coefficient times one full-dimensional source fiber. This assertion is scoped to positive (d)-volume; it does not discard intrinsic boundary mass in a (q<d) argument.

## 5. All moduli and parity budgets

For every positive integer (m), the exact relation is

\[
\Psi(u)-\Psi(v)\in m\Lambda_0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad u-v\in m\mathbb Z^n.
\]

Projection proves the forward implication. Conversely, for (m\ge2), the integer point (w=v+(u-v)/m) lies in the segment and therefore in (U). Its anchored representation forces

\[
f_j(u)-f_j(v)=m(f_j(w)-f_j(v)).
\]

The full graph difference is divisible by (m) in the ambient integer lattice, and its quotient lies in (E_0); hence it lies in (Lambda_0). The case (m=1) is immediate. This proves all moduli, not merely the seven-modulus test range.

Consequently the exact number (k(U)) of occupied parity classes survives the canonical lift, even if its lattice rank rises. Choosing any lattice basis preserves this quotient-lattice statement. Different dependence components cannot share a parity class: their midpoint would belong to (U), and its anchored two-point representation would join those components. Thus

\[
k(U)=\sum_i k(U_i).
\]

Closed minors have no more occupied classes than the larger set. Canonical lifting of each such minor preserves its own count. These are the precise properties needed in the reduction; paying (2^{\operatorname{rank}\Lambda_0}) is unnecessary.

## 6. Conditional attainment with target (gamma_d/k(U))

This transfer passes for (d\ge1), positive measured fibers, and a strict failing original family. It does not claim attainment of a dimension-free infimum over all bases.

First lift the failing family. Pulling back every original halfspace under the base projection shows that lifting can only decrease maximum depth, with the same fiber measures. Since (k(P)\le2^n), an OC violation is a strict (gamma_d/k(P)) violation. If the original source has additional zero-(d)-volume fibers, retaining only its positive fibers leaves its measure unchanged and restricts its candidate set, so this initial implication remains valid.

Select a smallest-cardinality bad canonical lifted closed minor from the finite minor collection. For a dependence decomposition, additivity of (k) supplies a component with (M_i/k_i\ge M/k). The exact restriction inequality

\[
D_U\ge(M_i/M)D_{U_i\text{ in }U}\ge(M_i/M)D_{\Phi(U_i)}
\]

makes that smaller component bad, a contradiction. Thus the selected base is connected.

Normalize a minimizing sequence to total mass one and pass to limiting fiber masses. Their positive support (T) is closed by the same translate-of-a-positive-source inclusion used above. If (T) were proper, its retained mass would tend to one, giving

\[
b_d(\Phi(T))\le\beta<\gamma_d/k(U)\le\gamma_d/k(T).
\]

This again contradicts smallest-cardinality choice. Hence all limiting masses are positive, with a uniform positive lower bound after discarding finitely many sequence terms.

The remaining cited compactness proof uses only that positivity and dependence connectivity, not the former Helly denominator. A determinant-one maximal-inscribed-simplex normalization bounds one anchor diameter. The positive-volume cone estimate propagates bounded diameters through every finite anchored hyperedge. The centroid array is then within bounded distance of (L(B)\otimes\mathbb R^d). On the canonical base every member of (L(B)) is affine, so subtracting that projected array is an actual ambient affine shear, not arbitrary fiber-dependent recentering. This bounds all positions without changing depth or compatibility.

Simultaneous Hausdorff limits preserve compatibility and positive volumes. Convex indicators converge in fiberwise (L^1), hence in total variation for the finite mixed measure. Within a fixed base, candidate displacement (delta) changes any cap with unit continuous normal by a slab of mass at most

\[
|U|\kappa_{d-1}R^{d-1}\delta.
\]

Pure-base caps are unchanged by such displacement. The uniform bound therefore includes arbitrarily oblique normals and all closed boundary caps. Total variation plus this Lipschitz bound passes the maximum depth to the actual limiting candidates. The attained depth is exactly ( eta).

Thus the corrected target gives an all-positive, dependence-connected, lattice-complete attained bad minimum, conditional on a strict positive-volume OC failure. No step proves that this minimum satisfies ( eta\ge\gamma_d/k(U)).

The additional primitive-triple consequence is also correct. A bad family's masses are all strictly below (M/k(U)), so (|U|>k(U)). A shortest same-parity pair has difference (2v) with primitive (v): otherwise the closer same-parity point obtained by dividing (v) lies in the segment and hence in (U). Its midpoint supplies the third consecutive lattice site. This supplies no additive cap-mass charging rule.

## 7. Executed exact certificates and scope

Reran, read, and checked:

* `supporting computation verify_unequal_three_site_finite_base_counterexample_root.py`: PASS, eight exact polygon cap masses, plane covers, and projective source arithmetic;
* `supporting computation verify_unequal_three_site_homothetic_counterexample_root.py`: PASS, nine exact cap masses and plane covers;
* `supporting computation verify_canonical_lift_lattice_parity_root.py`: PASS, seven exact supporting facets, exactly thirteen lifted integer points, rank increase (3\to4), eight occupied parity classes, and all pairwise congruences for moduli (2,\ldots,7).

The rational polygon clippers retain zero-margin vertices and use exact rational intersections; these closed-boundary conventions are valid. The lift verifier's bounded integer box contains the full hull and its exact facet enumeration covers every supporting facet. For the asserted canonical nature of that calibration, the supplied anchored-face description and (dim L(P)=5) calculation in `candidate e3932c47b953f7cd` were also checked. The general all-modulus and attainment claims rest on the proofs above, not on the finite verifier.

No OC conclusion follows from these results. The failed arbitrary-base target must remain closed, and the retained lattice completeness and occupied-parity budget are essential additional data for the remaining minimum.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
